Mononeuritis multiplex (asymmetric axonal neuropathy of >= 2 non-contiguous nerve trunks) is the neurologic hallmark of necrotizing systemic vasculitis (PAN, EGPA, GPA) caused by ischemic necrosis from epineurial arteriole necrotizing vasculitis.

Neuro-Behçet disease manifests parenchymally in 80% (brainstem-diencephalic syndrome with pyramidal/cerebellar signs) and non-parenchymally in 20% (cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, CVST); parenchymal disease is treated with high-dose steroids and anti-TNF or azathioprine.

Neurosarcoidosis exhibits predilection for basal meninges, producing cranial neuropathy VII (unilateral or bilateral Bell palsy in 50%), diabetes insipidus from hypothalamic-pituitary granulomas, and leptomeningeal enhancement on post-gadolinium MRI.

Central nervous system pachymeningitis (diffuse dural thickening with contrast enhancement sparing leptomeninges) is a characteristic complication of IgG4-related disease and ANCA-associated vasculitis (predominantly PR3-positive GPA).

Cervical myelopathy from atlantoaxial subluxation (AAS) in rheumatoid arthritis develops when pannus erodes the transverse odontoid ligament, producing anterior atlanto-dens interval (ADI) >3 mm in adults (>9 mm signals impending medullary compression).

topics.title: Cardiac involvement in rheumatic disease
mustKnow: Libman-Sacks endocarditis presents with sterile non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis (verrucous vegetations) on the left-sided heart valves (mitral > aortic) on both atrial and ventricular surfaces, heavily linked with high-titer antiphospholipid antibodies.

Rheumatoid arthritis accelerates ischemic atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease with a 1.5 to 2.0-fold increased risk of myocardial infarction; systemic inflammation (CRP, TNF-alpha) mediates endothelial dysfunction and plaque instability independently of traditional Framingham risk factors.

Cardiac amyloidosis (AL and wild-type/mutant ATTR) causes rapidly progressive restrictive cardiomyopathy with concentric biventricular thickening, low ECG voltage discordance with echocardiographic wall thickness >12 mm, and apical sparing pattern on global longitudinal strain strain echocardiography.

Complete congenital heart block (third-degree AV block) in neonatal lupus erythematosus results from transplacental passage of maternal anti-Ro/SSA (specifically 52-kDa Ro) and anti-La/SSB antibodies binding fetal L-type calcium channels leading to autoimmune myocarditis and AV nodal fibrosis.

Takayasu arteritis induces severe ostial coronary arteritis and thoracic ascending aortic dilation leading to aortic valve regurgitation and congestive heart failure in young females; monitored via 18F-FDG PET-CT and MR angiography.

Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) cardiac involvement carries the highest mortality (accounting for >50% of deaths) manifesting as eosinophilic myocarditis, endomyocardial fibrosis, and intracardiac apical mural thrombus.

Systemic sclerosis (SSc) primary myocardial disease involves patchy myocardial band necrosis and focal ischemia from 'cardiac Raynaud' phenomenon, culminating in myocardial fibrosis, ventricular tachyarrhythmias, and diastolic dysfunction on cardiac MRI late gadolinium enhancement.

Pericarditis with or without cardiac tamponade is the most common cardiac manifestation across SLE (up to 40-50% in autopsy series), adult-onset Still disease, and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis, presenting with low-voltage PR depression and diffuse ST elevation.

topics.title: Hypermobility and heritable connective tissue disorders
mustKnow: Beighton score >= 5/9 in adults (>= 6/9 in prepubertal children, >= 4/9 in adults >50 years) objectively defines generalized joint hypermobility (GJH); evaluates bilateral passive fifth finger hyperextension >90 deg, thumb opposition to forearm, elbow hyperextension >10 deg, knee hyperextension >10 deg, and trunk flexion palms to floor.

Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (hEDS, 2017 international criteria) is diagnosed clinically without definitive single-gene mutation, requiring generalized joint hypermobility, systemic manifestations of connective tissue disorder (>= 2 criteria groups), and absence of fragile skin or vascular fragility.

Vascular Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (vEDS, EDS type IV) is caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in COL3A1 encoding type III collagen; features extreme fragility of medium/large arteries, bowel rupture, gravid uterine rupture, and characteristic thin vermilion facial phenotype.

Classical Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (cEDS, EDS types I/II) is caused by mutations in COL5A1 or COL5A2 encoding type V collagen, characterized by marked skin hyperextensibility (>1.5 cm at volar forearm), widened atrophic papyraceous ('cigarette paper') scars, and joint hypermobility.

Marfan syndrome (revised Ghent nosology) is caused by dominant FBN1 mutations encoding fibrillin-1; core diagnosis requires aortic root enlargement (Z-score >= 2.0) and ectopia lentis (superotemporal lens subluxation), or systemic score >= 7 in presence of family history.

Loeys-Dietz syndrome is caused by mutations in TGF-beta signaling genes (TGFBR1, TGFBR2, SMAD3, TGFB2/3), characterized by the triad of arterial tortuosity/widespread aneurysms, hypertelorism, and bifid/cleft uvula.

Osteogenesis imperfecta (types I-IV) is caused by COL1A1/COL1A2 mutations in type I collagen, presenting with recurrent bone fractures with minimal trauma, blue sclerae, dentinogenesis imperfecta, and conductive/mixed hearing loss from stapes footplate fixation.

Arterial dissection screening and cardiovascular management in vEDS and Marfan include annual echocardiography/vascular MRA, avoidance of contact/isometric sports, and blood pressure control using celiprolol (vEDS) or beta-blockers/angiotensin receptor blockers (Marfan).

topics.title: Pregnancy and reproductive health in rheumatic disease
mustKnow: Preconception counseling in systemic lupus erythematosus mandates maintaining quiescent disease or low disease activity for at least 6 months prior to conception, which significantly reduces the risks of maternal disease flares, lupus nephritis relapses, preeclampsia, and preterm delivery.

Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is safe and strongly recommended to be continued throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding in all women with SLE; HCQ reduces maternal flare rates, lowers preeclampsia risk, and halves the recurrence risk of congenital heart block in anti-Ro/SSA-positive mothers.

Transplacental crossing of maternal anti-Ro/SSA (anti-Ro52/Ro60) and anti-La/SSB antibodies causes neonatal lupus erythematosus; the most severe permanent manifestation is congenital complete (third-degree) heart block, developing in 2% of primigravid anti-Ro positive mothers and recurring in up to 15% to 20% in subsequent pregnancies.

Serial fetal echocardiographic surveillance (pulsed Doppler monitoring of mechanical PR interval) is recommended weekly or biweekly from gestational weeks 16 to 26 in anti-Ro/SSA-positive pregnancies to detect early, potentially reversible first- or second-degree heart block.

Absolute teratogenic contraindications in pregnancy include methotrexate (fetal aminopterin-methotrexate syndrome with craniofacial and skeletal defects), mycophenolate mofetil (microtia, cleft palate, cardiac anomalies), cyclophosphamide, and leflunomide (requires cholestyramine washout before conception).

Immunosuppressive medications compatible with pregnancy and lactation include azathioprine (dose <=2 mg/kg/day), calcineurin inhibitors (cyclosporine, tacrolimus), and systemic glucocorticoids (prednisone <=20 mg/day, metabolized by placental 11-beta-HSD2 so minimal drug reaches the fetus).

Certolizumab pegol is a pegylated Fab fragment of an anti-TNF antibody that lacks an Fc region and cannot bind the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn); prospective pharmacokinetic trials demonstrate negligible placental transfer throughout all three trimesters, making it the preferred anti-TNF biologic in pregnancy.

Low-dose aspirin (75 to 150 mg daily) initiated before 16 weeks of gestation is recommended for all pregnant women with SLE or antiphospholipid antibodies to reduce the risk of maternal preeclampsia, placental insufficiency, and fetal growth restriction.

topics.title: Pediatric rheumatology beyond JIA
mustKnow: Childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus (cSLE, diagnosed before age 18) accounts for 15% to 20% of all SLE cases, exhibiting an aggressive disease phenotype with significantly higher rates of severe proliferative lupus nephritis (>50% to 60%), severe neuropsychiatric involvement, and higher cumulative glucocorticoid toxicity.

Juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) is the most common idiopathic inflammatory myopathy in childhood, characterized by pathognomonic heliotrope rash, Gottron papules, symmetrical proximal muscle weakness, and a distinctive prominent vasculopathy involving skin, muscles, and gastrointestinal tract.

Dystrophic calcinosis (calcinosis cutis and calcinosis universalis) complicates up to 30% to 40% of JDM cases, particularly in patients with delayed diagnosis, prolonged active unremitting inflammation, or anti-NXP2 autoantibodies, causing painful subcutaneous nodules, skin ulceration, and debilitating joint contractures.

Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) is a post-infectious hyperinflammatory syndrome developing 2 to 6 weeks following SARS-CoV-2 infection, characterized by persistent fever, shock, acute myocardial dysfunction, markedly elevated inflammatory markers (ferritin, CRP, D-dimer, troponin, NT-proBNP), and features overlapping with Kawasaki disease.

Chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis (CNO, also known as chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis, CRMO) is an autoinflammatory bone disorder of childhood presenting with recurrent episodes of sterile osteolytic bone pain and swelling, characteristically affecting the metaphyses of long bones, clavicle, and vertebrae, requiring whole-body MRI.

First-line therapy for CNO/CRMO relies on regular scheduled NSAIDs; patients with active spinal lesions or disease refractory to NSAIDs respond dramatically to intravenous pamidronate or zoledronic acid (bisphosphonates) or anti-TNF biologics, which resolve bone edema and prevent vertebral collapse.

Growth failure in pediatric rheumatic diseases results from a combination of chronic active systemic inflammation (IL-6 and TNF-alpha directly inhibiting the growth hormone/IGF-1 axis and epiphyseal chondrocyte proliferation) and prolonged exposure to high-dose systemic glucocorticoids.

Transition of adolescent patients from pediatric to adult rheumatology services requires a planned, structured multidisciplinary transition process initiated early (by age 13 to 14 years), fostering patient self-advocacy, medication autonomy, and preventing loss to follow-up during young adulthood.

topics.title: Rheumatic manifestations of malignancy and checkpoint inhibitors
mustKnow: Cancer-associated myositis occurs in up to 15% to 25% of adult dermatomyositis patients, with the highest risk of synchronous cancer within 3 years of myositis onset (especially in patients older than 50 years with anti-TIF1-gamma or anti-NXP2 autoantibodies), typically presenting as adenocarcinomas of the lung, ovary, breast, or gastrointestinal tract.

Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy (HOA, Pierre Marie-Bamberger syndrome) is characterized by the classic clinical triad of digital clubbing, bilateral symmetrical painful periostitis of tubular long bones, and synovial effusions, secondary to underlying intrathoracic malignancy (non-small cell lung cancer) or chronic cyanotic cardiopulmonary disease.

The pathophysiology of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy involves platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) released by unfragmented megakaryocytes that bypass pulmonary capillary filtration in cyanotic right-to-left shunts or are overexpressed by pulmonary tumor cells, driving subperiosteal neoangiogenesis and osteoblast proliferation.

Plain radiographs in hypertrophic osteoarthropathy demonstrate symmetric, smooth or laminated ('onion-skin') periosteal new bone formation along the diaphyses and metaphyses of distal tubular bones (radius, ulna, tibia, fibula), with 99mTc-methylene diphosphonate (MDP) bone scan displaying diffuse, symmetric 'double stripe' cortical uptake.

Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs targeting PD-1 [pembrolizumab, nivolumab], PD-L1 [atezolizumab], and CTLA-4 [ipilimumab]) trigger immune-related adverse events (irAEs); inflammatory arthritis occurs in 3% to 10% of treated patients, presenting as seronegative RA-like symmetrical polyarthritis or polymyalgia rheumatica-like syndrome.

Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myositis is an aggressive, life-threatening toxic emergency, characteristically presenting with acute necrotizing myopathy that frequently co-occurs with concomitant autoimmune myocarditis (causing refractory cardiogenic shock, arrhythmias) and myasthenia gravis-like ocular/bulbar weakness.

Management of severe ICI-induced rheumatic toxicity (Grade >=3 or life-threatening myositis/myocarditis) mandates immediate permanent discontinuation of the checkpoint inhibitor, immediate initiation of high-dose intravenous pulse methylprednisolone (1 g daily for 3 days), with early addition of abatacept, IVIG, or infliximab.

RS3PE (remitting seronegative symmetrical synovitis with pitting edema) is a benign elderly-onset syndrome characterized by bilateral symmetric polyarthritis, severe tenosynovitis with striking dorsal hand and foot pitting edema, negative RF, and dramatic responsiveness to low-dose glucocorticoids, but warrants thorough malignancy screening as it can present as a paraneoplastic manifestation.

topics.title: Glucocorticoids in rheumatology
mustKnow: Glucocorticoids exert therapeutic effects via classical genomic mechanisms (cytosolic glucocorticoid receptor homodimerization and nuclear transactivation or transrepression of NF-kappa-B and AP-1) and rapid non-genomic mechanisms (membrane receptor signaling and physicochemical intercalation into cell membranes).

Comparative glucocorticoid equivalent dosages, anti-inflammatory potencies, and mineralocorticoid potencies: hydrocortisone 20 mg (potency 1, mineralocorticoid 1), prednisone 5 mg (potency 4, mineralocorticoid 0.8), methylprednisolone 4 mg (potency 5, mineralocorticoid 0.5), and dexamethasone 0.75 mg (potency 25 to 30, mineralocorticoid 0).

High-dose intravenous pulse methylprednisolone (typically 500 to 1,000 mg daily infused over at least 60 minutes for 3 consecutive days) saturation of cytosolic receptors engages rapid non-genomic anti-inflammatory pathways; cardiac monitoring is indicated during infusion due to risks of sudden cardiac arrhythmias and fatal cardiovascular collapse.

Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis suppression should be assumed in any patient receiving prednisone >20 mg/day for >3 weeks, any patient receiving an evening dose of >5 mg prednisone for >3 weeks, or anyone with a clinical Cushingoid appearance, mandating gradual tapering to permit adrenal recovery.

Stress-dose glucocorticoid coverage is required during major surgical stress, acute trauma, or critical illness in patients with HPA axis suppression: hydrocortisone 50 to 100 mg intravenously immediately, followed by 50 mg every 8 hours (or 200 mg continuous infusion daily) with rapid tapering as physiological stress resolves.

Osteonecrosis (avascular necrosis, AVN) of bone is a severe dose- and duration-dependent adverse effect of glucocorticoid therapy; the femoral head is the most frequent anatomical site (bilateral in >70%), presenting with groin pain aggravated by weight-bearing, with MRI demonstrating the diagnostic 'double line sign' on T2-weighted images.

Antimicrobial prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) with oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (one single-strength tablet daily or one double-strength tablet three times weekly) is strongly recommended for patients receiving prednisone >=20 mg/day for >=4 to 8 weeks combined with a second immunosuppressant.

Primary prevention of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) with oral bisphosphonates (alendronate, risedronate) or IV zoledronic acid is recommended for all adults aged >=40 years at moderate-to-high fracture risk who anticipate long-term glucocorticoid therapy (prednisone >=2.5 mg/day for >=3 months).

topics.title: Cytotoxic and immunosuppressive agents
mustKnow: Cyclophosphamide is an oxazaphosphorine alkylating prodrug converted by hepatic CYP2B6/CYP3A4 into 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide, which spontaneously breaks down into active phosphoramide mustard (which cross-links DNA strands at guanine N-7 positions) and toxic acrolein.

Acrolein concentrates in the bladder lumen, causing chemical mucosal ulceration and acute hemorrhagic cystitis, and multiplies the long-term risk of transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder; co-administration of sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate (mesna) and vigorous hydration neutralizes acrolein into a non-toxic thioether adduct.

Cyclophosphamide induces dose-dependent premature ovarian failure (amenorrhea) and azoospermia, with risk escalating dramatically above a cumulative lifetime dose of 10 to 15 g and advancing female age; co-administration of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists (leuprolide) during treatment significantly preserves ovarian reserve.

The Euro-Lupus regimen (low-dose IV cyclophosphamide: 500 mg every 2 weeks for 6 doses, total 3 g) demonstrated equivalent long-term renal remission and significantly lower rates of severe infections and gonadal toxicity compared to the high-dose NIH regimen (0.5 to 1 g/m2 monthly for 6 months).

Tacrolimus binds intracellular FK-binding protein 12 (FKBP12), and cyclosporine binds cyclophilin; both complexes inhibit the phosphatase activity of calcineurin, preventing nuclear translocation of NFAT (nuclear factor of activated T cells) and blocking IL-2 gene transcription.

Voclosporin is a next-generation semi-synthetic calcineurin inhibitor featuring an altered carbon-1 carbon-single-bond side chain that increases calcineurin-binding potency 3- to 4-fold without altering elimination; it demonstrates a predictable pharmacokinetic profile that eliminates the need for routine therapeutic drug monitoring.

Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) removes pathogenic circulating autoantibodies, immune complexes, and cryoglobulins from the plasma volume; recognized ASFA Category I indications in rheumatology include catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome, Goodpasture (anti-GBM) disease with alveolar hemorrhage, and thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP).

High-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG, 2 g/kg total dose administered over 2 to 5 days) exerts multimodal immunomodulatory effects: blockade of Fc-gamma receptors on macrophages, neutralization of autoantibodies by anti-idiotypic networks, enhanced clearance of pathogenic IgG via saturation of FcRn, and inhibition of complement activation.

topics.title: Novel immunotherapies and cell therapy
mustKnow: CD19-targeted chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy achieves profound, deep immune system 'reset' in refractory severe systemic lupus erythematosus, idiopathic inflammatory myositis, and systemic sclerosis by comprehensively eliminating tissue-resident and circulating autoreactive B cells and plasma cell precursors, producing drug-free sustained remission.

Anifrolumab is a fully human IgG1kappa monoclonal antibody directed against subunit 1 of the type I interferon receptor (IFNAR1); it blocks downstream phosphorylation of STAT1/STAT2 induced by all type I interferons (IFN-alpha, IFN-beta, IFN-omega), FDA/EMA-approved for moderate-to-severe SLE with prominent cutaneous and musculoskeletal efficacy.

Avacopan is an orally administered, highly selective competitive small-molecule antagonist of the human complement C5a receptor (C5aR1/CD88); in the phase 3 ADVOCATE trial, avacopan successfully replaced high-dose systemic glucocorticoids in ANCA-associated vasculitis, improving renal eGFR and minimizing steroid-related toxicities.

Obinutuzumab is a type II glycoengineered anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody that induces enhanced direct non-apoptotic cell death and superior antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) compared to type I antibodies (rituximab); the NOBILITY phase 2 trial proved that obinutuzumab significantly enhanced complete renal response in proliferative lupus nephritis.

Telitacicept is a recombinant dual-target fusion protein consisting of the TACI receptor extracellular domain fused to human IgG1 Fc; it simultaneously neutralizes both B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS/BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), suppressing abnormal B-cell and plasma cell maturation in SLE and rheumatoid arthritis.

Deucravacitinib is an oral, first-in-class selective allosteric inhibitor of tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) that binds to the unique regulatory pseudokinase (JH2) domain, inducing conformational allosteric receptor inactivation; it potently blocks signaling of IL-23, IL-12, and type I interferons without inhibiting JAK1, JAK2, or JAK3.

Dapirolizumab pegol is an investigational pegylated Fab' fragment targeting CD40 ligand (CD40L/CD154) that lacks an Fc domain (eliminating past risks of platelet activation and thromboembolism), blocking critical T-cell/B-cell costimulation in systemic lupus erythematosus.

Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitors (such as fenebrutinib and remibrutinib) selectively inhibit downstream B-cell receptor (BCR) and Fc-receptor signaling in B lymphocytes and myeloid cells, undergoing advanced phase 3 evaluation for refractory systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjogren disease, and chronic spontaneous urticaria.

topics.title: NSAIDs, colchicine and analgesics
mustKnow: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) inhibit cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2), blocking the conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandins; constitutive COX-1 maintains gastric mucosal protection and renal blood flow, while inducible COX-2 drives inflammatory pain, fever, and vascular endothelial prostacyclin (PGI2) synthesis.

The landmark PRECISION trial evaluated cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, and renal safety among 24,000 osteoarthritis and RA patients; moderate-dose celecoxib (100 to 200 mg daily) demonstrated non-inferiority to prescription naproxen and ibuprofen for cardiovascular events, with significantly lower gastrointestinal bleeding events.

Nephrotoxic mechanisms of NSAIDs stem from inhibition of vasodilatory prostaglandins (PGE2 and PGI2) that normally preserve renal blood flow and GFR during hypovolemia or heart failure; acute NSAID use triggers prerenal acute kidney injury via afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction, hyperkalemia (hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism), and acute interstitial nephritis.

All NSAIDs (with the possible exception of low-dose naproxen) increase the risk of myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure exacerbations, and systemic hypertension, caused by selective or non-selective suppression of endothelial COX-2-derived anti-thrombotic prostacyclin without concomitant suppression of platelet COX-1-derived pro-thrombotic thromboxane A2.

Colchicine exerts its primary anti-inflammatory mechanism by binding unpolymerized tubulin heterodimers, inhibiting microtubule polymerization and elongation; this disrupts neutrophil chemotaxis, lysosomal degranulation, phagocytosis, and suppresses activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome.

The AGREE trial established that low-dose colchicine (1.2 mg immediately followed by 0.6 mg 1 hour later, total 1.8 mg over 1 hour) achieves equivalent pain reduction to high-dose regimens (4.8 mg over 6 hours) in acute gout flares, while exhibiting a favorable gastrointestinal adverse effect profile indistinguishable from placebo.

Colchicine is metabolized hepatically by CYP3A4 and actively exported by the P-glycoprotein (ABCB1) efflux transporter; co-administration of strong CYP3A4 or P-glycoprotein inhibitors (clarithromycin, erythromycin, ketoconazole, cyclosporine) in renal or hepatic impairment causes fatal colchicine toxicity (neuromyopathy, bone marrow aplasia, shock).

Low-dose colchicine (0.5 mg daily) exerts vascular cardioprotective benefits: the LoDoCo2 and COLCOT randomized trials demonstrated that low-dose colchicine significantly reduced major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke) in chronic coronary disease and post-myocardial infarction.

topics.title: Infection screening and vaccination in immunosuppression
mustKnow: Screening for latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) with an interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA: QuantiFERON-TB Gold Plus or T-SPOT.TB) and a baseline chest radiograph is mandatory prior to initiating any biologic DMARD or targeted synthetic DMARD (JAK inhibitor).

When latent tuberculosis infection is identified, targeted preventive therapy (e.g., oral rifampin 600 mg daily for 4 months, or once-weekly isoniazid 900 mg plus rifapentine 900 mg for 12 weeks, or isoniazid 300 mg daily for 9 months with pyridoxine) must be initiated, with biologic initiation delayed for at least 1 month after starting therapy.

Serological screening for Hepatitis B virus (HBsAg, anti-HBc total, anti-HBs) is mandatory prior to immunosuppressive therapy; in patients who are HBsAg-positive or anti-HBc-positive receiving B-cell depleting therapy (rituximab), prophylactic antiviral therapy with entecavir or tenofovir must be started before rituximab and continued for at least 12 to 18 months post-depletion.

Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) chemoprophylaxis with oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (one single-strength tablet daily or one double-strength tablet three times weekly) is indicated for patients receiving high-dose glucocorticoids (prednisone >=20 mg daily for >=4 to 8 weeks) combined with another immunosuppressant, or cyclophosphamide therapy.

Live-attenuated vaccines (measles-mumps-rubella [MMR], varicella, yellow fever, oral polio, live attenuated zoster) are strictly contraindicated in patients receiving biologic agents, targeted synthetic DMARDs, or high-dose systemic glucocorticoids due to the risk of uncontrolled vaccine-strain viral replication.

Recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) is an adjuvanted non-live subunit vaccine that is strongly recommended for all patients aged >=50 years, and for immunocompromised patients aged >=18 years, administered as a two-dose intramuscular series 2 to 6 months apart, safe to administer during immunosuppressive therapy.

Pneumococcal vaccination is strongly recommended for all patients on immunosuppression using the 20-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV20) alone, or the 15-valent conjugate vaccine (PCV15) followed >=8 weeks later by the 23-valent polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23), administered prior to immunosuppression whenever feasible.

B-cell depleting therapy with rituximab markedly blunts humoral immune responses to vaccines; non-live vaccines should ideally be completed at least 2 to 4 weeks prior to rituximab infusion, or delayed until at least 5 to 6 months after the last rituximab dose when peripheral B cells begin reconstituting.

topics.title: Drug toxicity monitoring
mustKnow: Methotrexate monitoring mandates baseline complete blood count, serum creatinine, and liver transaminases (AST, ALT); monitoring is repeated every 2 to 4 weeks during dose escalation, then every 8 to 12 weeks during stable maintenance, withholding methotrexate if transaminases exceed 2- to 3-fold the upper limit of normal.

Leflunomide requires regular blood pressure monitoring at every clinical visit because it causes or exacerbates systemic arterial hypertension in up to 10% of patients through sympathetic nervous system activation, alongside routine monthly-to-quarterly liver function tests.

Hydroxychloroquine retinopathy screening (per AAO 2016 guidelines) requires baseline fundus examination and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) within the first year, followed by annual automated 10-2 visual fields and SD-OCT after 5 years of use (or earlier if daily dose exceeds 5.0 mg/kg actual body weight or renal impairment exists).

JAK inhibitors (tofacitinib, baricitinib, upadacitinib) carry boxed regulatory warnings based on the ORAL Surveillance trial for increased incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), venous thromboembolism (deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism), serious infections, and malignancies (especially lymphoma and lung cancer).

Tocilizumab and sarilumab (IL-6 receptor antagonists) cause dose-dependent elevation of circulating lipid parameters (total cholesterol, LDL, triglycerides), mild transient neutropenia, and an increased risk of lower gastrointestinal tract diverticular perforation, requiring baseline and periodic lipid profiles and immediate evaluation of acute abdominal pain.

Anti-TNF agents are strictly contraindicated in patients with moderate-to-severe congestive heart failure (NYHA Class III or IV) or reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (<50%) based on clinical trials showing increased heart failure hospitalizations and cardiovascular mortality.

Anti-TNF therapy is strongly contraindicated in patients with a personal or first-degree family history of multiple sclerosis or central nervous system demyelinating disease, as TNF inhibitors can induce new-onset or exacerbate preexisting optic neuritis, transverse myelitis, and demyelination.

Calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, cyclosporine) require routine therapeutic drug monitoring (target 12-hour trough levels) and serial serum creatinine and potassium measurements due to dose-dependent afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction causing acute nephrotoxicity, chronic interstitial fibrosis, and hyperkalemia.

topics.title: Rheumatologic emergencies
mustKnow: Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome (CAPS) is an acute medical emergency presenting with multiorgan microvascular thrombosis involving >=3 organs over <1 week; immediate treatment requires emergency triple therapy: intravenous pulse methylprednisolone (1 g daily for 3 days), therapeutic parenteral anticoagulation (heparin), and plasma exchange or IVIG.

Scleroderma renal crisis (SRC) is an acute hypertensive emergency characterized by malignant hypertension, rapid oliguric acute renal failure, and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia; emergency therapy requires prompt initiation and upward titration of short-acting ACE inhibitors (oral captopril) with blood pressure gradually reduced over 48 to 72 hours.

Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH) in pulmonary-renal syndrome manifests with hemoptysis, acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates, and an abrupt drop in hemoglobin with increased diffusing capacity (DLCO); urgent bronchoscopy with sequential bronchoalveolar lavage shows progressively bloodier aliquots and hemosiderin-laden macrophages.

Atlantoaxial subluxation with cervical myelopathy in rheumatoid arthritis presents with occipital pain radiating to the vertex, Lhermitte sign, spastic quadriparesis, and hyperreflexia; an anterior atlanto-dens interval (AADI) >3 mm on flexion lateral cervical radiographs confirms instability, and posterior-atlantodental interval (PADI) <=14 mm indicates imminent spinal cord compression requiring urgent neurosurgical stabilization.

Giant cell arteritis with acute visual loss or transient amaurosis fugax represents an ophthalmic emergency; intravenous pulse methylprednisolone (500 to 1,000 mg daily for 3 consecutive days) must be administered immediately prior to temporal artery biopsy to prevent bilateral irreversible anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.

Macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) is a secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) complicating systemic JIA or adult-onset Still disease; clinical hallmarks include unremitting fever, falling ESR with extreme hyperferritinemia (>10,000 ng/mL), consumptive hypofibrinogenemia, thrombocytopenia, and hemophagocytosis on bone marrow biopsy, treated urgently with pulse steroids, anakinra, or cyclosporine.

Native joint bacterial septic arthritis is an orthopedic emergency causing enzymatic chondrolysis and irreversible joint destruction within 24 to 48 hours; urgent needle arthrocentesis must be performed for synovial analysis and culture, followed immediately by empiric intravenous bactericidal antibiotics and complete joint decompression.

Acute lupus myocarditis manifests with unexplained resting tachycardia, gallop rhythm, acute congestive heart failure, and cardiogenic shock, with cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial edema on T2 and diffuse late gadolinium enhancement; urgent management requires intravenous pulse methylprednisolone combined with cyclophosphamide or IVIG.

topics.title: Disease activity and outcome measures
mustKnow: In rheumatoid arthritis, composite disease activity indices guide treat-to-target adjustments: DAS28 (evaluating 28 joints, ESR/CRP, and patient global) defines remission as <2.6 and low disease activity as <=3.2; Clinical Disease Activity Index (CDAI, which excludes laboratory tests) defines remission as <=2.8 and low disease activity as <=10.0.

Simplified Disease Activity Index (SDAI) incorporates 28 tender and swollen joint counts, patient and physician global assessments (0 to 10 cm VAS), and C-reactive protein (mg/dL); an SDAI score <=3.3 defines stringent remission, aligning closely with the ACR/EULAR Boolean 2.0 remission definition.

ACR20, ACR50, and ACR70 response criteria are standardized clinical trial endpoints requiring >=20%, >=50%, or >=70% improvement in both tender and swollen joint counts, plus >=20%, >=50%, or >=70% improvement in at least 3 of 5 core variables (patient global, physician global, pain VAS, HAQ-DI disability, and acute-phase reactants).

The Health Assessment Questionnaire Disability Index (HAQ-DI) assesses functional physical disability across 20 activities in 8 categories, scored from 0 (no disability) to 3 (completely disabled); a change of >=0.22 points represents the universally accepted minimal clinically important difference (MCID).

In axial spondyloarthritis, disease activity is measured by the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI, 0 to 10 scale, with >=4 defining active disease) and the Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score (ASDAS, incorporating CRP/ESR), where ASDAS <1.3 denotes inactive disease, 1.3 to <2.1 moderate activity, 2.1 to <=3.5 high activity, and >3.5 very high activity.

In systemic lupus erythematosus, SLEDAI-2K evaluates 24 weighted organ items over the preceding 30 days, where a score >=6 denotes clinically active disease requiring therapy modification, and a score <=4 is required to fulfill the Lupus Low Disease Activity State (LLDAS).

In systemic necrotizing vasculitis, the Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS version 3) evaluates 64 items across nine organ systems, distinguishing new/worse persistent manifestations from chronic irreversible damage, which is independently tracked using the Vasculitis Damage Index (VDI).

In psoriatic arthritis, Minimal Disease Activity (MDA) is defined as fulfilling at least 5 of 7 outcome criteria: tender joints <=1, swollen joints <=1, PASI <=1 or body surface area <=3%, patient pain VAS <=15 mm, patient global VAS <=20 mm, HAQ-DI <=0.5, and tender entheseal points <=1.

topics.title: Landmark trials in rheumatology
mustKnow: The BeSt trial in early rheumatoid arthritis compared four treat-to-target treatment strategies, proving that initial combination therapy with csDMARDs plus a tapered glucocorticoid bridging or methotrexate plus infliximab produced faster functional improvement and significantly halted radiographic joint damage compared to sequential monotherapy.

The ORAL Surveillance randomized post-marketing safety trial in RA patients aged >=50 years with >=1 cardiovascular risk factor demonstrated that tofacitinib failed non-inferiority to TNF inhibitors, conferring higher hazard ratios for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and malignancies, driving major regulatory labeling revisions.

The RAVE trial in severe ANCA-associated vasculitis established that B-cell depletion with rituximab (375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 doses) was non-inferior to oral cyclophosphamide for remission induction at 6 months, and was significantly superior in the subgroup presenting with relapsing disease.

The PEXIVAS trial, the largest randomized trial in ANCA-associated vasculitis (704 patients), showed that routine therapeutic plasma exchange did not reduce all-cause mortality or end-stage renal disease in severe AAV with renal impairment or alveolar hemorrhage, while a reduced-dose glucocorticoid regimen was non-inferior to standard-dose with fewer serious infections.

The ADVOCATE trial demonstrated that avacopan (oral complement C5a receptor antagonist, 30 mg twice daily) was non-inferior to prednisone taper at 26 weeks and superior in sustained remission at 52 weeks in ANCA-associated vasculitis, significantly improving renal recovery and eGFR without steroid-associated toxicity.

The BLISS-LN trial demonstrated that adding intravenous belimumab (10 mg/kg) to standard-of-care induction (mycophenolate mofetil or Euro-Lupus cyclophosphamide) in active lupus nephritis significantly increased Primary Efficacy Renal Response (43% vs 32% at week 104) and halved the risk of renal-related events or death.

The SENSCIS trial proved that the oral intracellular tyrosine kinase inhibitor nintedanib (150 mg twice daily) reduced the annual rate of forced vital capacity (FVC) decline by 44% compared to placebo in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD), gaining regulatory approvals.

The CARES and FAST randomized cardiovascular safety trials evaluated allopurinol versus febuxostat in gout: CARES reported higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality with febuxostat, but the larger, prospective European FAST trial (6,128 patients) demonstrated that febuxostat was non-inferior to allopurinol regarding cardiovascular death, MACE, and all-cause mortality.
